sources.entry: FreeDisplay - Control external display brightness, HiDPI modes, resolution, and arrangement from the menu bar. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/hakanotal/FreeDisplay) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: FreeDisplay is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that provides many of the core display-control features of the paid BetterDisplay app, including brightness, HiDPI modes, resolution, arrangement, color profiles and night mode.
summary.what_it_does: It controls external monitor brightness over DDC/CI (IOKit on Intel, IOAVService on Apple Silicon), falling back to software dimming through the gamma table when DDC is not answered. It controls built-in and Apple display backlights through DisplayServices, and intercepts keyboard brightness keys to route them to the display under the cursor. It lets you browse and switch display modes including HiDPI, add HiDPI modes to external monitors via override files in /Library/Displays, and drag displays to arrange them with edge snapping. It also switches ICC color profiles per display, applies image adjustments (contrast, temperature, RGB, invert), provides a night mode blue-light filter on a schedule, and can create virtual displays through the CGVirtualDisplay private API. Presets save and restore full display configurations, and the app can launch at login and restart after a crash. The UI is available in Turkish and English.
use_cases: control external monitor brightness from the menu bar
enable HiDPI or Retina modes on an external monitor
arrange multiple displays and set the main display
switch ICC color profiles per monitor
reduce blue light with a night mode schedule
create a virtual display on a Mac
how_to_run: Option 1: download the latest FreeDisplay .dmg from GitHub Releases and drag FreeDisplay.app to Applications
First launch: open the app, then allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/FreeDisplay.app)
Option 2: git clone the repository, then cd FreeDisplay
Run ./scripts/build-dmg.sh to produce build/FreeDisplay.app and a DMG
Xcode is optional; the script works with Command Line Tools (xcode-select --install)
Grant Accessibility permission for brightness key interception
notable: Free alternative to BetterDisplay's paid Pro features, with no third-party dependencies
Per-monitor DDC channel matching by vendor, model, serial and name, with coalesced commands
Software gamma fallback for monitors that do not respond to DDC, such as some USB-C docks
Brightness key interception via a CGEventTap that routes keys to the display under the mouse cursor
Explicitly excludes EDID override, screen streaming and XDR/HDR extra brightness
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later; uses private APIs (CGVirtualDisplay, DisplayServices).
The app is not notarized, so macOS blocks the first launch and Accessibility permission may need to be re-granted after updates.
HiDPI changes need an administrator password and HiDPI modes appear only after the monitor reconnects.
